## 4 · Demand deep dive — scripts, persistence, coverage offset

- **Scale:** IQVIA — 4x early Ozempic/Wegovy prescribers at 12 months post-launch, rising patients-per-provider; Zepbound #1 weight-management Rx (Jan 2026 cut, 94% US data); KwikPen smoothing fill; ex-US KwikPen ~8M (2024) → ~25M (2026).
- **Supply:** aggregate shortage over — tirzepatide off FDA list since Dec 2024, all injectable GLP-1 adequate by Feb 2026 — but dose-strength fill stays uneven; with pharmacy-level stockouts concentrated in specific strengths rather than blanket shortage; constraint shifted from absolute shortage to mix management.
- **Coverage (the bear's best fact):** — a 12pp tightening even as revenue grew ~48% — employer GLP-1 cover 72% (2025) → 60% (2026); growth funded by cash-pay, prior-auth navigation, LillyDirect vials ($299–449/dose) — willingness-to-pay proven, volume ceiling capped until coverage stabilizes.
- **Verdict:** US injectable tight-balanced (~$14.9B Q2 incretin quarter, +45–91% YoY legs) (dose-mix risk); oral capacity-led upside; covered access capped; OUS device-constrained growth; share defended 12m, Amgen threat back-loaded past late-2027.

:::

## 5 · Oral pipeline — optionality with early receipts

Orforglipron (Foundayo: $98M Q2 after April US launch; UK sales from Aug 24, 2026) is the highest-variance leg. File: first small-molecule oral GLP-1 through Phase 3 (Apr 2025: A1C −1.3 to −1.6%, −16.0 lbs/−7.9% top dose); third P3 win (Aug 2025) → global obesity filings (40+ countries by Apr 2026); ACHIEVE-3 head-to-head win over oral semaglutide (Feb 2026, The Lancet); obesity ~−12.4% at 72w (36 mg), no food/water restriction. Small-molecule scale (~600 Da, continuous reactors; with no titration complexity and primary-care scalability; Huntsville integration + $3B Netherlands oral plant) underwrites volume. Bear's fair cut: 12.4% vs 20%+ segments oral to needle-averse/maintenance; GI tolerability + daily adherence historically compress oral value; Novo's oral Wegovy + amycretin (−13.1%, 12w P1) contest convenience directly. Hedge: retatrutide — all-dose P3 obesity wins at 80w (May 2026), diabetes A1C to −2% / −16.8%, −22 to −24% at 68w non-diabetic, seven more 2026 readouts — extends (Dec 2025: seven additional 2026 readouts guided; filing date unannounced) — extends the injectable frontier if oral underwhelms on magnitude.

![Efficacy ladder. Zepbound 20.2% anchors the injectable lead; orforglipron 12.4% is an access play](charts/efficacy.png){#fig-ex8 width=90%}


## 6 · Competition map — bracketed but not yet breached

Novo attacks on three axes: oral Wegovy pill (convenience), amycretin dual GLP-1/amylin (−13.1%, 12w, early), CagriSema (22.7% filed; only major obesity asset under FDA review; Q4 2026 decision) — the top competitive binary of the next twelve months. — the top competitive binary of the next twelve months, directly attacking both convenience and max efficacy. Amgen's MariTide (16–20% at 52w P2, monthly dosing, post-stop maintenance, higher top-dose GI; six P3s running + three T2D P3s in 2026) attacks adherence from the interval flank, commercial risk concentrated late-2027+. commercial risk concentrated late-2027 and beyond rather than inside this report's window. Lilly's moat is observed: SURMOUNT-5 (n≈700) Zepbound 20.2% vs Wegovy 13.7% at 72w — a gap buying prescriber inertia and switching costs — plus unreplicable-in-12m manufacturing and 40+ oral filings in train. Verdict: defended share, bracketing trajectory (convenience below, efficacy above, adherence sideways); any hierarchy repricing compresses the multiple — none has yet.

## 7 · Manufacturing and capacity — a $30B moat that must be filled

Committed: ≥$27B across four new US sites (Texas + Virginia mega-sites, Pennsylvania anchor, Puerto Rico upgrade; Pleasant Prairie $3B GLP-1 expansion Dec 2024) + $3B Netherlands oral plant (~500 hires) ≈ $33B stack for supply-led growth — fill-finish, KwikPen/auto-injector, hybrid peptide synthesis (plug-flow, nanofiltration, PAT), Huntsville small-molecule integration. Filled = deepest moat in the note (no rival matches device+molecule+geography in 12m; OUS syringe/vial→KwikPen curves pace on this capacity). OUS launch curves (syringe/vial bridging to KwikPen by geography upon approval) pace directly on this capacity releasing. Unfilled = the bear's FCF anchor (depreciation + opex drag for years). Q2 says filling: volume-led growth, off-shortage aggregate, OUS +80%, early oral receipts. Three tells: strength-level fill-rate, KwikPen conversion by geography, capex-guide revisions.

![Capex stack. ~USD 33B committed; bull reads moat, bear reads fixed-cost leverage — tie-break is fill-rate, currently filling.](charts/capex.png){#fig-ex9 width=90%}

## 12 · Bull versus bear — adjudicated

Bull's three survivors: (a) ~$92B annualized run-rate above an $85–87B guide funds beat-and-raise; (b) OUS +80% plus small-molecule oral scale = genuine second/third engines; (c) SURMOUNT-5's 6.5-pt gap + ~$30B capacity = 12-month share moat. Bear's three survivors: (a) ~30x leaves no miss room; skew −27% vs +25%; (b) 72%→60% coverage proves narrowing access, cash-pay selects affluence; (c) CagriSema Q4 + oral/amycretin + monthly MariTide bracket every flank. Adjudication: bull takes the base (revenue, filings, launches, capacity observed; kills contingent) — bear takes sizing (30% × −27% with gaps → ≤2% into events, 2–4% aggregate). Demotions: Verzenio/Kisunla cushion (no math), Demotions from the debate: the Verzenio/Kisunla diversification claim (demoted — no cushion math), LillyDirect-as-solution (partial offset — cash caps volume), capex-moat (conditional on fill-rate).
